episode_title: Inside the Mind of a Venture Capitalist Who's Good at TikTok, with Andrew Chan, Managing Partner and Founder of ATAS VC

real_qa.q: What is ATAS VC's investment thesis and what industries does the firm focus on?
real_qa.r: ATAS VC is a pre-seed focused venture firm investing in American necessities real technologies to solve real problems for real people. The firm backs pre-seed companies working across energy, manufacturing, agriculture and other core American industries, focusing on hard tech—applied robotics, complex AI, and technology with engineering risk rather than existential science risk where the core science is already validated.
real_qa.requete: ATAS VC investment thesis focus industries

real_qa.q: Why did Andrew Chan leave Builders VC to start his own venture capital firm?
real_qa.r: Chan left Builders VC because they were moving toward growth equity and Series A investing, which he wasn't enjoying. He took time off for personal reasons and realized there was a fundamental lack of good science in venture capital, especially on the deep tech side, with insufficient scientific underwriting standards. He found himself in a stable cash position and able to take risk, so he started ATAS VC to build a firm with higher scientific standards and less focus on hype wave fundraising.
real_qa.requete: Andrew Chan leave Builders VC start ATAS VC why

real_qa.q: What is the difference between hard tech and deep tech venture investing according to Andrew Chan?
real_qa.r: Chan distinguishes hard tech from deep tech by focusing on engineering risk rather than science risk. He avoids investing in quantum or fusion where existential questions remain about feasibility. Hard tech investments require validated science but may have scalability challenges—the question is whether throwing more engineering talent at the problem will eventually solve it, not whether the core science fundamentally works.
real_qa.requete: hard tech vs deep tech venture capital difference

real_qa.q: What are Andrew Chan's publicly disclosed investments through ATAS VC?
real_qa.r: Chan has three public investments through ATAS VC: a mining technology and automation company, a wireless power grid optimization company, and a wireless spectrum infrastructure company. The firm is roughly one year old as of the interview.
real_qa.requete: ATAS VC portfolio investments mining wireless power

real_qa.q: What was Andrew Chan's first major angel investment exit and when did it occur?
real_qa.r: Chan's first big angel exit was with GPT-0 (an AI detection company) approximately one month before the interview. The investment was made right when ChatGPT came out, and three years later it became his first major exit as an angel investor.
real_qa.requete: Andrew Chan GPT-0 angel exit AI detection

guest.bio_context: Andrew Chan is a former NASA JPL scientist with a Bachelor of Science in Geophysics and English Literature from Caltech. He spent six years in institutional venture capital, most recently at Builders VC before founding ATAS VC, a pre-seed focused venture firm. He previously worked at the Denver Zoo for four years and has built internal AI systems using GPT technology during the early adoption phase.

real_quote: I think there's a fundamental lack in venture capital of good science, especially on the deep tech side—I don't invest in something where existentially we have no idea if it's feasible or not.
